verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere's own Mintlify API reference has a "Try it" playground on its endpoint pages, generated from a published OpenAPI 3.1.0 document, so users can run requests interactively. Coverage is limited: the reference spans only the hosted Wally cloud API, not the on-device SDKs. Running examples needs the caller's own key against the production gateway, with no test keys, mock mode, or isolated sandbox documented. missing for 10: interactive reference coverage of the on-device SDK APIs, a sandbox or test-key mode for safely running examples, independent or hands-on corroboration of the playground.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: The Mintlify API reference runs the "Try it" playground on the endpoint pages, generated from the OpenAPI document.
RunAnywhere publishes a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1.0 document for its hosted inference API
Executing requires the caller's own key and runs against the production gateway.
